data.content_ref: inline:Verisimilitude as a Regulative Ideal (92968bc0cf42d965) reduces to the methodological commitment that science aims at truth rather than certainty. This relation is refuted if it can be shown that the concept of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) cannot be formally defined without implicitly relying on inductive probability, thereby making the shift from probability to verisimilitude merely a semantic disguise for the very induction Popper rejected.
